course:
Although I took the course knowing what the structure will be like, I still think that the arrangement is faulty. The content of this course MUST be divided into two separate courses. I think Michele hoca handled the course content as best as possible. But I always felt that there is not enough time for either of Landscape Archaeology or ArcGIS lab. I believe Landscape Archaeology is not a topic that you can be knowledgeable at it (let alone being good at it) with only one hour per week, it is simply not possible. If these were two separate classes, both Landscape A. and ArcGIS could have been taught in more depth. I don't think that what we have learned in this course can make you proficient at distribution analysis, movement analysis, and so on. At best, you can learn (in the ArcGIS part of the course) how to make maps that can be published in articles. But as I said, this is because there was not enough time to learn ArcGIS in depth. That was disappointing. 

I would suggest there should be a separate course called ___GIS. Moreover, a second/advanced class for GIS is also a must, if the department really wants to teach students GIS.

The weakest aspect is that the course required us to learn a new software which was very exciting but the instructor could not manage to teach it well  which led to low marks in exams. The strongest aspect is that the course was very interesting and helped gain a new skill.
